newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's local money market opened flush with cash on Tuesday with short-term interest rates quoted mostly softer in active trade, dealers said.

The central Reserve Bank forecast an end-of-day surplus of Z$292 million, and auctioned 91-day treasury bills amounting to Z$300 million at 24.24 percent to mop up the excess money. This was down from the 24.32 percent average rate for treasury bills sold on Monday.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought on Tuesday at 26 percent from 26.5 percent the previous day and sold another half a percentage point lower at 24.5 percent.
Bankers acceptances dropped to 25 from 25.5 percent (buying) and to 24.25 percent on the selling side from 24.30 percent while call money held steady at 24 percent.
